solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Type of building predominant in Devon

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in the county of Devon, standing for the town itself

parts.note: a barn is a type of farm building
staple means main or chief, as in a staple diet

explanation.surface: A remark about which kind of building is most common across the Devon countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'in Devon' points to a town that lies in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a market town on the north coast of the county of Devon in England.

clue.text: Suffer when Genoa is destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the letters of the preceding words are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed when the Italian city of Genoa is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to feel great anguish, a synonym for suffer.

clue.text: Acclaimed books Edward acquired

indicators.note: acquired means the name for Edward takes in the books, holding them inside

parts.note: Ned is a familiar short form of Edward
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A man named Edward picked up some highly praised books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward' suggests ED or TED, but the short form needed here is the other familiar one.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means famous or well known, a synonym of acclaimed.

clue.text: Group after record for slimming

indicators.note: after places the word for group behind the word for record in the answer

parts.note: to tape is to record, and a tape is a recording
a ring is a group, such as a ring of smugglers

explanation.surface: A band follows up its album with a diet plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapering is narrowing gradually, getting slimmer towards one end.

clue.text: Request reliable cooker or vessel

parts.note: a plea is a request or appeal
sure means dependable, as in a sure bet
a steamer is a pan for cooking food by steam

explanation.surface: A kitchen shopping request: a dependable cooking appliance or some kind of pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a kitchen container beside 'cooker'; it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boat carrying passengers on trips for enjoyment, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: The French rejected uniform for soccer team

indicators.note: rejected means the French article is turned back, read in the opposite direction in this down clue

parts.note: le is French for the
even means uniform, regular, unvarying

explanation.surface: The French turned down a kit for their football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' sends the French article backwards; 'uniform' looks like a football kit but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer side fields this many players, so the number is a common name for the team.

clue.text: Mike works and cleans up

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ops, short for operations, are works, as in musical opuses

explanation.surface: A man called Mike has a job doing the cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mops is wiping floors clean, so the verb means cleans up.

clue.text: Assistant keeps wine cold for champ

indicators.note: keeps means the word for assistant holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a mate is an assistant, as in a plumber's mate
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A helper hangs on to chilled wine for the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' looks like a champion; here it is the verb meaning chew noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to chew vigorously, and masticating is chewing.

clue.text: Obtain expert remedy

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is an expert
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Get hold of a cure from a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to get or acquire it.

clue.text: Excited about nothing? That's a laugh!

indicators.note: about means the word for excited wraps around the zero

parts.note: hot can mean excited or worked up
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Getting worked up over nothing is just funny.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is something very funny, so calling a thing a hoot says it is a laugh.

clue.text: Show anxiety before changing places

indicators.note: changing places says the two parts swap, so the order the clue gives them in is reversed

parts.note: tension is nervous strain or anxiety
pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Displaying nerves before moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is not an order word here but a synonym; 'changing places' then swaps the two parts the clue lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretension is affected display or ostentation, a sense of show.

clue.text: Theologian in last stand — one wanting a lot

indicators.note: in means the theologian is placed inside the word for last stand

parts.note: a bier is the stand a coffin rests on, a body's last stand
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A religious scholar making a final stand against someone greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last stand' suggests a final fight, but it is a coffin stand. 'a lot' is an item at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, a person who makes offers is trying to win an item, called a lot.

clue.text: Misleading promise to wear glasses

indicators.note: to wear puts the promise inside the glasses, as if dressed in them

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
an IOU (I owe you) is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: A deceptive pledge to put on spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially plausible but actually wrong, so it misleads.

clue.text: An inventor does, when about to endorse an agreement

indicators.note: about means the word for does goes around the signing

parts.note: does are female deer, so deer stands for does
to sign is to endorse an agreement with a signature

explanation.surface: An inventor does something when about to sign a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb but is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer creates new things, so is an inventor of products or styles.

clue.text: Being nervous, indisposed a prankster

parts.note: ill means indisposed, unwell
a tease is someone who mocks or plays tricks

explanation.surface: A practical joker who is uneasy and off sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling uncomfortable or anxious is the idiom's meaning, matching nervousness.

clue.text: By no means all stage directors are elderly

indicators.note: By no means all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that only some theatre directors are old.
explanation.definitionFit: Being old is being elderly, so 'are aged' and 'are elderly' match.

clue.text: Faulty doorbell in disorderly house

indicators.note: faulty suggests something broken, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken bell at the front door of a messy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorderly house' reads as an untidy home but is an old legal term for a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordello is a brothel, which the law historically called a disorderly house.

clue.text: Tory leader has pain in bum

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: to ail is to cause pain or trouble

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's chief complaint is in the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain in bum' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail is slang for the buttocks, the same body part as bum.

clue.text: Sat awkwardly on transport that's in question

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of the previous word are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: to take is to transport or carry

explanation.surface: Someone sat uncomfortably on a vehicle which is being queried.
explanation.definitionFit: When a matter is at stake it is the thing at issue, the point under consideration.

clue.text: Learned about colour many years ago

indicators.note: about means the word for learned surrounds the colour

parts.note: sage means wise or learned
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Someone well read discussing colour from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when tools were made of rock lies thousands of years in the past.

clue.text: Man carries weapon in clothing

indicators.note: carries means the word for man holds the weapon within it

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a man
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A man has a gun hidden in his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is a single article of clothing.

clue.text: Rehabilitate engineer with a criminal record

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
form is British slang for a criminal record

explanation.surface: Getting an engineer with past convictions back on track.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform an offender is to correct their behaviour, which is what rehabilitating aims at.

clue.text: Wears tie loosely, so to speak

indicators.note: loosely suggests letters arranged freely, so the preceding words are shuffled

explanation.surface: He wears his tie loose, if you can put it that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms signalling that words are used figuratively.

clue.text: Old fool makes a full stop approaching a road

indicators.note: approaching places the full stop just ahead of the rest

parts.note: a dot is a full stop, the punctuation mark

explanation.surface: A senile man halts just before reaching a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is an old person whose mind has weakened with age.

clue.text: Mark's suspicion

definitions.meaning: a sign or vestige left behind, as in a mark leaving no sign
a slight hint or tinge, as in a suspicion of garlic

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sign left behind and a faint amount, a suspicion of something.

clue.text: Father managed moral development in a mystic way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining an adjective: of a supernatural, unexplained kind

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: development suggests change, so the letters of the neighbouring word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad oversaw someone's spiritual growth in a mysterious manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Supernatural events beyond scientific explanation are described as mystic or occult.

clue.text: Confirm or 'esitate

definitions.meaning: to assert or declare to be true
haver, Scots for hesitate, with its H dropped as the apostrophe shows

explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly, and haver without its H means to dither.

clue.text: Plain water

definitions.meaning: simple, nothing more than, as in a plain formality

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning simply or only and a noun for a lake.

clue.text: "I'm to enter a new arrangement" articulated performer

indicators.note: a new arrangement signals the preceding letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An entertainer announces they will join a new show.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings has jointed limbs and performs on stage.
